agent_answer.notes: Only three corpus papers (S004, S014, S019) report latency; all others (S001-S003, S005-S013, S015-S018, S020) do not measure or report latency for LLM-generated answers, so they provide no evidence on this question. Latency in each paper is defined as the mean number of seconds to produce one answer. The three papers give conflicting directions: S004 shows retrieval-augmented (retrieve-then-read) generation slower, S014 shows it faster, and S019 shows it faster on one dataset (TriviaCheck) and slower on the other (HistoryQuest). Thus the corpus answer is that RAG does change latency, but the sign of the change depends on the setup. Supporting claims: claim-000001..claim-000015.

cells.conclusion: Yes. Retrieval-augmented generation changes the latency of LLM-generated answers, but the direction is not consistent across the papers. In S004 the retrieve-then-read model is slower than the parametric-only model on both datasets (LawFactQA 3.47s vs 2.74s; GeoFacts 3.21s vs 1.57s). In S014 the retrieval-augmented model is faster than the closed-book model on both datasets (BioClaimQA 1.12s vs 1.16s; TriviaCheck 0.94s vs 1.96s). In S019 the retrieve-then-read model is faster than the no-retrieval baseline on TriviaCheck (1.09s vs 1.91s) but slower on HistoryQuest (2.63s vs 1.99s).
